A''' writing system''' was in common use throughout the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] and continued to be used during the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. It seems to contain upside-down [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]] characters as well as other characters with a similar appearance to those found within the Aurebesh script.

==Known use==
This script was commonly used to display information on small, portable devices. This script displayed targeting information on [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell's]] [[Electro-goggles/Legends|electro-goggles]]<ref name="Portfolio">{{WebCite|url=http://Principiagraphica.com/portfolio.htm|text=Philip Metschan's portfolio|archivedate=20110715113025}}</ref><ref name="Holographic Artist">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/feature/20020716/indexp2.html|text=''Holographic'' Artist: Philip Metschan}}</ref> and [[KiSteer 1284 projectile rifle/Legends|sniper rifle]] optics.<ref name="AotC">{{Film|II}}</ref>

It also displayed information on the display screens of the [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7 ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor]] belonging to the prominent Jedi [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]].

[[File:Plokoonjsf.png|thumb|left|180px|[[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170]] console displaying information using this writing system]]

The [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170 starfighter]] that shot down [[Plo Koon's Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Plo Koon's Delta-7 starfighter]] was kitted out with this script at the time of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]].

[[File:Vos_Gesal_Street.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Scrolling holofeed on Vos Gesal Street]]
Information feeds displayed information in this script on [[Vos Gesal Street/Legends|Vos Gesal Street]] and throughout the wider [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Uscru Entertainment District]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the data readouts in [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] private office utilized this script, which Palpatine had been reading when [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] arrived to inform him that General Obi-Wan Kenobi was about to fight General [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]].<ref name="RotS">{{Film|III}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The script (which lacks an [[in-universe]] name) is an in-universe writing system further developed by [[Philip Metschan]], based upon an earlier [[Joe Johnston]] typeface developed for the [[Original trilogy]]. Although Metschan states that "The actual font set hadn't been used since [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|the first ''Star Wars'']],"<ref name="Holographic Artist" /> it does not appear in the completed film. Its only appearances on screen in the Original Trilogy are in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], where it appears on a variety of screens aboard the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|Death Star II]] and [[Star Destroyer]]s, as well as in the [[Endor shield generator bunker|shield generator bunker on the forest moon]]. Metschan's version of the typeface can be seen throughout [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']].<ref name="Portfolio" /><ref name="Holographic Artist" />

Fans will have difficulty transliterating this font, as Metschan only canonized the letters A through U.<ref name="Holographic Artist" /><ref name="Portfolio" />

The script is also visible on [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Obi Wan's Jedi Starfighter]] cockpit display screens and Zam Wesell's [[KiSteer 1284 projectile rifle/Legends|KiSteer 1284 projectile rifle]] scope display in ''Attack of the Clones''.<ref name="Portfolio" /><ref name="Holographic Artist" />
